messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging maya-oncall, samir-eng — High error rate (502/503) observed for customer 'Tideway Health' running in Dedicated Pool PHX-2. Impact: request failures and elevated latency >5s. Correlation with KV cache spikes.
maya-oncall: On it. Can someone confirm scope — only Tideway affected?
samir-eng: Confirmed — metrics show failures only for pool PHX-2 tenants where Tideway routes. Other pools normal.
neha-sre: Adding logs to thread. Starting login into nodes now.
eli-ops: Noted — traffic from Tideway was 3x baseline starting 02:12 UTC, many long-history chats. Could be KV cache growth.
katie-cs: @maya can you badge this as customer-impacting? Tideway CS and their SRE are already paging for status.
maya-oncall: Yes flagged. @acct-ops please prepare to discuss SLA impact.
acct-ops: On it. If outage >30m we'll likely owe pro-rata credits per SLA. Need exact downtime window.
samir-eng: Quick snapshot of the error from the frontend: ``ERROR: 500 downstream OOM at serve_worker.cpp:1423 — kv_cache_alloc failed size=1.9GB``. Looks like serving processes hit memory hard limits and started returning 5xx.
neha-sre: On a node: ``top`` showed rss for model-worker peaking at 12GB on 16GB host, swap thrash.
ryan-ciso: Any sign of cross-tenant memory bleed or data leakage? Priority question from Tideway security.
samir-eng: No evidence of cross-tenant access in logs. Processes are isolated per container. We'll double-check core dumps.
eli-ops: Immediate mitigation proposal: 1) Evict KV cache for Tideway (soft eviction) 2) Failover traffic to fallback pool in us-west for a subset 3) Scale up PHX-2 nodes by adding 2 spare instances temporarily. Can we do 1 now?
maya-oncall: Execute step 1. Neha, can you run eviction script?
neha-sre: Running: ``/opt/redwood/bin/kvcache evict --tenant tideway --policy soft --confirm``
neha-sre: Eviction started — cache size dropping. Latency dropping in metrics. Errors still present but decreasing.
samir-eng: Pushing a quick config to cap per-tenant KV growth: ``kv_cache.max_per_tenant=512MB`` (hotfix). Rolling to PHX-2 nodes.
eli-ops: Routing test: spinning up route to fallback pool now — sanity traffic routed to fallback small-model variant.
katie-cs: I just told Tideway CS team we implemented mitigation and are routing to a fallback. They want an ETA for full restore.
maya-oncall: ETA for stabilization ~15-20m, full service back in ~45-60m after restarts.
acct-ops: Noted start of customer-impact window at 02:12 UTC. Recording for SLA.
samir-eng: Root-cause hypothesis (prelim): token distribution spike from long chat sessions caused unbounded kv-cache growth in our new dynamic-kv caching path. This combined with increased batch size on PHX-2 led to memory pressure and OOMs.
ryan-ciso: Please confirm no PII leaked. Also prepare statement for Tideway security describing isolation guarantees.
samir-eng: Confirming container-level isolation held. We'll provide logs and the `dmesg`/audit traces.
pm-lucas: Heads-up — Tideway exec wants a live phone in 30m. Can we get an aggregate timeline and mitigation summary?
katie-cs: I'll draft an executive summary. Starting: "We detected elevated errors — routed traffic to fallback, evicted caches, applied per-tenant caps, and added capacity. No evidence of data exposure." Will share draft here.
neha-sre: Restarting the two most affected workers sequentially to reclaim memory.
eli-ops: Scaling complete: 2 extra instances added to PHX-2, autoscaler paused to avoid oscillation.
samir-eng: After hotfix rollout and restarts, 5xx rates down to baseline. Watching for regressions.
maya-oncall: Great. After we stabilize, need a coordinated customer follow-up: 1) RCA draft 2) Exec-level note 3) SLA credit calc 4) Postmortem internal w/ timeline and the patch to kv_cache. Assign owners?
katie-cs: I'll own customer comms + exec note.
acct-ops: I'll calculate SLA credit and draft the billing note.
samir-eng: I'll own technical RCA and patch PR. Plan to push full fix (rate-limited kv growth + telemetry) in next release.
neha-sre: I'll do the incident timeline and runbook updates.
ryan-ciso: I'll review the security summary and sign off for customer.
pm-lucas: Ops/Eng to prepare a 5–10 min executive brief for Tideway call.
maya-oncall: Good. Please keep updates in this thread. Postmortem meeting scheduled tomorrow 15:00 UTC.
katie-cs: Draft customer executive note (first pass):
``
Hi Tideway team,

We wanted to follow up on the service disruption you experienced at 02:12 UTC today. Summary: Our serving runtime hit memory pressure for your dedicated pool (PHX-2) due to unusually large KV cache growth driven by a spike in long-history chats. Immediate actions we took: evicted KV cache for your tenant, routed a portion of traffic to a fallback pool, applied a temporary per-tenant KV cap, and added capacity. Service returned to baseline within ~40 minutes.

Impact: Some requests returned 5xx and latency was elevated during the window. No evidence of data access between tenants. We are preparing a Root Cause Analysis and permanent fix, and will provide an executive write-up and proposed SLA credit within 24 hours.

Sincerely,
The Redwood Ops team
```
maya-oncall: Good. Add estimated credits and timeline once acct-ops has numbers.
acct-ops: Preliminary SLA calc: 40m of partial outage -> estimate 0.028 day's credit on monthly committed billing for Tideway. I'll provide exact figure in 1 hour.
samir-eng: I'll attach the initial PR link once opened: ``https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4821`` (prelim). It contains: cap enforcement, telemetry for per-tenant kv size, and a test harness.
ryan-ciso: Sharing the security blurb to include in comms: "No cross-tenant data access observed; root cause was resource exhaustion within a tenant's worker process. We retain audit logs and are happy to share relevant extracts under NDA"
katie-cs: Sending draft to Tideway contact now and scheduling exec call.
maya-oncall: Closing note: create formal RCA doc in docs/incident-postmortems after meeting. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
